scope: Actual full17 lower_teddy_to_rim geometry; all proposed translations and final lowering are frozen hypotheses, not physical continuations
limitations: Captured body sections are material surfaces at one actual time, not rigid apertures. Cloth expands/deforms under subsequent contact.
Frozen teddy contour sample inside fractions are unweighted discrete boundary-point diagnostics, not volume fractions or continuous fit guarantees.
Plane cuts are closed only below actual lowest rim; upper mouth contact and gripper/robot routes require separate checks.
No native contact, force, strain, grip or dynamics were executed for any candidate.
Root owns robot preflight and final choice.

bounded_comparison_conclusion.condition: Only if root confirms the complete robot center/insert/release/withdraw preflight; this report executes none of those motions.
bounded_comparison_conclusion.reason: Largest COM contact-envelope margin (10.484 mm) and highest frozen teddy cut-point inside proportion (83.12%); minimum body-section COM clearance 7.25 mm is essentially tied with -15/-60 at7.36 mm. It has the shortest commanded XY displacement among these three.
bounded_comparison_conclusion.tradeoff: -15/-60 gives the best section-centroid alignment and smaller worst frozen protrusion (58.43 mm versus66.68 mm), but only3.815 mm contact-envelope COM margin. -15/-55 is intermediate in protrusion, with lower minimum body COM clearance and only4.688 mm envelope margin.
bounded_comparison_conclusion.actual_aperture_caveat: All three remain outside the actual ordered rim XY projection. These are deformable-contact candidates, never proofs of free passage or eventual containment.
